Maya — thanks for the diagram. I've pulled together a short "activation playlist" that teams tend to run through before our activation window. The playlist is intentionally ordered for fast verification and to avoid back-and-forth during the maintenance window. High level:

1) Account & access prep
   - Confirm Redwood service account created in your IAM with role: redwood-infra-activation
   - Pre-share KMS public key or KMS principal for key-wrapping access (we'll need an owner-level contact)

2) Network & routing
   - Egress: allow outbound to 52.36.0.0/16 (control plane) and 13.59.0.0/16 (metrics) on TCP/443
   - Inbound: ephemeral only for health probes from our monitoring subnet (we'll provide /28)
   - Ports: 8800 (gRPC), 443 (control), 8142 (agent telemetry)
   - MTU: 9000 recommended for NVLink nodes; 1500 acceptable otherwise

3) Node readiness
   - GPU driver versions, container runtime (containerd >= 1.6), kernel tuning (vm.max_map_count >= 262144)

4) Security & compliance
   - KMS access test vector + audit log forwarding to your SIEM (optional but recommended)
   - Service account credential rotation window set to <= 30 days for the activation period

5) Smoke validation (pre-activation)
   - Ping control plane endpoint, pull small model artifact, run single inference loop
   - Verify KV cache persistence across restart (if configured)

I've attached a lean markdown checklist (redwood_activation_playlist.md) that you can paste into your runbook. Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT to walk the list and nominate the on-call network engineer.

Attachment: redwood_activation_playlist.md

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[attachment: redwood_activation_playlist.md]
